content.content:
1	# Mise: build spec for a hands-free pantry-to-plate cooking app
2	
3	This SPEC.md specifies **Mise** (working name; rename freely), a Next.js web app built at HackCamp 2026 (nwPlus, UBC Vancouver, Nov 7–8, 2026). Users sign in with **Auth0**, add groceries by barcode, keep a per-user pantry with quantities and expiry dates in **Tiger Data** (TimescaleDB/Postgres), and get **real recipes found online by Gemini**, ranked toward whatever expires soonest. The original recipe is always shown first with attribution; an "AI-adapted" variant appears only when an ingredient is missing. Users cook hands-free with **MediaPipe** webcam gestures (scroll, next/previous step, timer, read aloud), with steps read aloud by **ElevenLabs** and `speechSynthesis` as the fallback. Finishing a recipe deducts what was used from the pantry and logs calories and protein in one database transaction. The app is served over HTTPS from a **Vultr** VPS, which the camera requires. The spec is written so three Claude Code accounts can build it in parallel through **Entire**. A Phase 0 foundation freezes the contracts in `src/contracts/`, the SQL schema and the stubs. After that, three workstreams (Cook Mode, Pantry & Nutrition, Recipes & Cooking Backend) each own separate directories, and an integration phase merges them. Researched facts are cited inline. Anything not confirmed against a primary source in research is marked **[VERIFY]**, and the open items are collected in §17. Treat those as the first things to check, not as settled.
4	
5	---
6	
7	## 0. How to use this document
8	
9	- **Who reads this:** three Claude Code agents (one per teammate account) plus the humans steering them. Each agent reads §1–§8 (shared ground truth), its own workstream in §18, and the relevant feature sections in §9.
10	- **Source of truth order:** `src/contracts/**` (code) > this SPEC > comments. If the SPEC and the contracts disagree after Phase 0, the contracts win. Raise the mismatch with a human; don't silently diverge.
11	- **Markers:** **[VERIFY]** = not confirmed against a primary source during research; check before relying on it. **P0** = required for the demo, **P1** = should have, **P2** = stretch.
12	- Anthropic's guidance for specs like this: "The most useful specs are self-contained: they name the files and interfaces involved, state what is out of scope, and end with an end-to-end verification step." Keep CLAUDE.md short ([Claude Code best practices](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/best-practices.md)). This spec follows both.
13	
14	---
15	
16	## 1. Overview, goals and non-goals
17	
18	### 1.1 Problem and pitch
19	
20	Home cooks waste food they forgot they had, and following a recipe on a phone or laptop with wet, floury hands is awkward. Screens dim and you lose your place. Mise closes the loop: **scan groceries → know what expires → cook a real recipe that uses it → touch nothing while cooking → pantry and nutrition update themselves.** HackCamp's challenge is to "identify a problem facing a community and build a solution that makes a meaningful difference". Judging covers Problem & User Research, Innovation, Technical Implementation, Design & UX, and Presentation ([HackCamp 2026 Devpost](https://hackcamp-2026.devpost.com/)).
21	
22	### 1.2 Goals (all confirmed by the team)
23	
24	| # | Goal | Priority |
25	|---|---|---|
26	| G1 | Web app: Next.js App Router + TypeScript, deployed on Vultr over HTTPS | P0 |
27	| G2 | Auth0 login. Every pantry item, recipe, session and meal belongs to one user | P0 |
28	| G3 | Tiger Data (TimescaleDB/Postgres) as the only database | P0 |
29	| G4 | Add groceries by barcode, scanned with the camera or typed. Lookup chain: **dataandapis.com → Open Food Facts → Gemini reads a product/label photo → manual form** | P0 |
30	| G5 | Expiry date from a photo of the printed date (Gemini reads it, user confirms) or typed in | P0 |
31	| G6 | Pantry tracks quantities and expiry dates, and deducts ingredients after cooking | P0 |
32	| G7 | Gemini finds **real recipes online**, shown **original-first with source attribution**, ranked to prefer items closest to expiry | P0 |
33	| G8 | Only when an ingredient is missing, AI may propose an adaptation, clearly marked **"AI-adapted"** and kept separate from the original | P0 |
34	| G9 | MediaPipe hand gestures: scroll up/down, next/previous step, start/pause step timer, read step aloud | P0 |
35	| G10 | Read aloud with ElevenLabs, falling back to browser `speechSynthesis` | P0 |
36	| G11 | Nutrition per pantry item and per recipe serving. Strict, code-enforced diet/allergy filters. Daily calorie and protein tracking | P0 |
37	| G12 | Meals logged through a "Finish cooking" prompt (servings eaten) and through manual logging | P0 |
38	| G13 | Built by 3 Claude Code accounts collaborating through Entire (Sessions, Graph, Brain, Trails) | P0 |
39	
40	### 1.3 Non-goals (explicitly out of scope)
41	
42	- Native mobile apps. PWA install/offline mode is also out (the site should still work in mobile browsers).
43	- Writing recipes from scratch with AI. The AI only *finds* recipes and *adapts* them when ingredients are missing.
44	- Medical or dietetic advice, or certified allergen guarantees. The app filters strictly but tells users to check labels.
45	- Shopping lists, grocery ordering, price tracking, meal planning calendars.
46	- Sharing pantries between users or households, and any social features.
47	- Contributing products back to Open Food Facts, which would need an OFF account for writes ([OFF API intro](https://openfoodfacts.github.io/openfoodfacts-server/api/)).
48	- Voice *commands* (speech recognition) are P2 only. The P0 hands-free channel is gestures plus read-aloud.
49	- Moving gesture inference to a Web Worker (P2; see §11.7).
50	- Hosted vector search or "similar recipes" (P2).
51	
52	### 1.4 Glossary
53	
54	- **Original recipe:** the recipe exactly as parsed from the publisher's page (schema.org `Recipe`), with attribution. Never modified.
55	- **AI-adapted recipe:** a separate object that references an original and lists explicit substitutions for missing ingredients.
56	- **Base units:** grams (mass), millilitres (volume), `count` (pieces). Every stored quantity uses one of them.
57	- **GTIN:** the canonical 13-digit (or 14-digit) barcode key. UPC-A is left-padded with `0`.
58	- **FEFO:** first-expired-first-out, the rule for choosing which pantry row to deduct from.
59	- **Armed:** the gesture state in which commands are accepted. Users arm it by holding an open palm.
60	
61	---
62	
63	## 2. User flows
64	
65	Each flow lists its happy path, then its branches. Feature IDs (F#) refer to §9.
66	
67	### UF1: Sign in and onboarding (F1)
68	1. A visitor lands on `/`. The marketing hero has a "Sign in" button that links to `/auth/login` (Auth0 Universal Login).
69	2. After callback, the first authenticated request upserts a `users` row keyed by Auth0 `sub`.
70	3. If `onboarded_at` is null, redirect to `/onboarding`. There the user sets diets (vegetarian, vegan, gluten-free, dairy-free, high-protein), allergens, daily kcal and protein goals (optional), and time zone (default `America/Vancouver`).
71	4. The user lands on `/today`.
72	
73	### UF2: Add a grocery by barcode (F2, F4, F5)
74	1. `/pantry/add` opens the camera scanner, with the **"Type barcode" input always visible**.
75	2. A code is accepted after 2 identical consecutive reads and a valid check digit. The client calls `POST /api/products/lookup`.
76	3. **Found** (cache, dataandapis or OFF): show a confirmation card with name, brand, image, nutrition per 100 g, package size, and source attribution ("Data: Open Food Facts, ODbL").
77	4. The user sets quantity (pre-filled from package size when known) and unit, then sets expiry: **"Photo of date"** (UF4) or **"Enter date"** or "No date".
78	5. Save. The item appears in `/pantry`, sorted by soonest expiry.
79	- **Branch, not found:** "We couldn't find this product." → **"Take photo of product & nutrition label"** (UF3) → if that fails or is declined → **manual form**. The manual form is reachable from every step.
80	- **Branch, provider down** (401/402/429/5xx/timeout): treated as a miss for the user, logged server-side. The flow continues to OFF, then to the photo step.
81	
82	### UF3: Product from a label photo (F3)
83	1. The user captures 1–3 photos (front, nutrition panel, optional side). The client downscales them to about 1600 px on the long edge, JPEG q≈0.85.
84	2. `POST /api/vision/label` → Gemini returns a draft and the server runs sanity checks.
85	3. The manual form opens **pre-filled**. Flagged fields are highlighted. The user must press **Confirm** before anything is saved (`userVerified=true`).
86	
87	### UF4: Expiry date from a photo (F4)
88	1. The user takes a close photo of the printed date.
89	2. `POST /api/vision/expiry` → the server assembles a date from Gemini's components and cross-checks it with a CFIA regex.
90	3. A date picker opens pre-filled, with the raw text shown ("Read: `BB/MA 2026 NO 15`"). If the order is ambiguous, the user picks from the candidates. **The user must confirm.** "Packaged on" dates are never accepted as expiry; instead the UI says "This looks like a packaged-on date".
91	
92	### UF5: Find recipes (F6, F7, F10)
93	1. `/recipes` shows chips for expiring-soon items (≤ 3 days, pre-selected) and a "Find recipes" button. The user's diet/allergy filters appear as locked chips with a link to Settings.
94	2. `POST /api/recipes/search` streams progress ("Searching the web… / Reading 8 recipe pages… / Checking your allergies…"), then candidate cards arrive one by one.
95	3. Each card shows the title, the **source site and author**, coverage ("You have 7 of 9 ingredients"), the expiring items it uses (badge "uses spinach, expires in 2 days"), missing-ingredient count, ≈kcal and protein per serving, and total time.
96	4. Candidates that break a diet or allergy filter never appear. A collapsed "N recipes hidden by your filters" note lists them by reason (no recipe content shown).
97	
98	### UF6: Recipe detail, original first, optional adaptation (F8, F9, F10)
99	1. `/recipes/[recipeId]` shows the **Original** card first: title, "From {siteName} by {author}", a "View original" link, ingredients exactly as published (each marked have / missing / staple), steps, and nutrition (our estimate with coverage, plus "Publisher's nutrition" if the page provided it).
100	2. If the recipe has missing ingredients, a secondary button reads **"Suggest an AI adaptation using my pantry"**. Pressing it calls `POST /api/recipes/[id]/adapt`. The result appears in a **separate card with an "AI-adapted" badge** on a different background. It lists substitutions ("Missing: buttermilk → Using: Greek yogurt + lemon (from your pantry)"), changed steps, warnings, and re-estimated nutrition.
101	3. "Cook original" and "Cook AI-adapted" (when present) are separate buttons, each with a servings stepper.
102	
103	### UF7: Cook hands-free (F11, F12, F13)
104	1. "Cook" → `POST /api/cook/sessions` → `/cook/[sessionId]`. The **"Start cooking" tap** unlocks audio and requests a screen wake lock.
105	2. One step per screen, in large type. The step's ingredients and quantities are listed and timer chips are docked at the bottom.
106	3. A **"Hands-free" toggle** loads MediaPipe lazily, asks for camera permission, and shows the HUD with a gesture legend. Open palm (hold) arms the system. Then swipe = next/previous, thumb up/down (hold) = scroll, fist (hold) = timer start/pause, victory sign (hold) = read step aloud / stop.
107	4. Each control also has big tap targets and keyboard shortcuts.
108	5. Refreshing or reopening the page offers "Resume at step 5?". Timers continue correctly because they are stored as absolute end times.
109	
110	### UF8: Finish cooking (F14)
111	1. On the last step (or any time from the menu) → **"Finish cooking"** dialog.
112	2. The dialog shows **Servings cooked** (default = planned), **Servings you ate** (default 1; 0 allowed), and a **deduction preview** with one line per matched pantry item ("Spinach: 150 g of 200 g → 50 g left"). Lines are editable and can be unchecked. Lines the app couldn't convert are flagged "Adjust manually". The nutrition for the servings eaten is editable.
113	3. Confirm → one transaction deducts the pantry, writes pantry events, inserts the meal log and closes the session → navigate to `/today` with a toast ("Logged 1 serving · 540 kcal · 32 g protein").
114	
115	### UF9: Daily tracking and manual logging (F15)
116	1. `/today` shows kcal and protein rings against the goals, today's meals list, a 7-day bar chart, and "Expiring soon" pantry items.
117	2. **"Log food"** offers three tabs: *From pantry* (pick item + amount; "Also remove from pantry" checkbox, default on), *Scan* (barcode → product → amount), *Quick add* (label + kcal + protein).
118	3. The user can delete a meal from today's list.
119	
120	---
121	
122	## 3. Architecture
123	
124	### 3.1 System diagram
125	
126	```
127	                         ┌──────────────────────── Browser (HTTPS secure context) ─────────────────────────┐
128	                         │  Next.js client components                                                        │
129	                         │  ┌──────────────┐  ┌───────────────────┐  ┌──────────────┐  ┌──────────────────┐ │
130	                         │  │ Scanner       │  │ Cook mode UI      │  │ Voice player │  │ Today / Pantry / │ │
131	                         │  │ BarcodeDetector│  │ steps, timers,    │  │ <audio> +    │  │ Recipes pages    │ │
132	                         │  │ (native or    │  │ wake lock, resume │  │ speechSynth  │  │                  │ │
133	                         │  │ zxing-wasm)   │  │ (localStorage)    │  │ fallback     │  │                  │ │
134	                         │  └──────┬───────┘  └───────┬───────────┘  └──────┬───────┘  └────────┬─────────┘ │
135	                         │         │      ┌───────────┴────────────┐        │                   │           │
136	                         │         │      │ GestureController      │        │                   │           │
137	                         │         │      │ MediaPipe tasks-vision │  camera frames NEVER leave the device  │
138	                         │         │      │ (WASM, self-hosted)    │        │                   │           │
139	                         │         │      └────────────────────────┘        │                   │           │
140	                         └─────────┼────────────────────┼───────────────────┼───────────────────┼───────────┘
141	                                   │ fetch (JSON / multipart / NDJSON / audio)                    │
142	┌──────────────────────────────────▼────────────────────▼───────────────────▼───────────────────▼───────────┐
143	│ Vultr VPS (Ubuntu, Docker)                                                                                │
144	│  Caddy 2 (TLS via Let's Encrypt, :80/:443)  ──reverse_proxy──►  Next.js standalone (Node 22) :3000        │
145	│                                                                  ├─ src/proxy.ts → auth0.middleware()     │
146	│                                                                  ├─ /auth/* (Auth0 SDK routes)            │
147	│                                                                  ├─ /api/* route handlers (Node runtime)  │
148	│                                                                  │    requireUser() on every handler      │
149	│                                                                  └─ src/server/** domain logic            │
150	└───────┬───────────────┬──────────────────┬──────────────────┬──────────────────┬──────────────┬──────────┘
151	        │               │                  │                  │                  │              │
152	        ▼               ▼                  ▼                  ▼                  ▼              ▼
153	   Auth0 tenant   Tiger Cloud        dataandapis.com     Open Food Facts     Gemini API     ElevenLabs
154	   (Universal     (Postgres +        Barcode Lookup      v2 product API      (grounded      TTS stream
155	    Login)        TimescaleDB,       (X-Api-Key)         (custom UA)         search, vision, (xi-api-key)
156	                  us-east-1)                                                  JSON output)
157	                                                                                   │
158	                                                                                   ▼
159	                                                                        Publisher recipe pages
160	                                                                        (server-side fetch →
161	                                                                         schema.org Recipe JSON-LD)
162	```
163	
164	Key properties:
165	- **All third-party keys live on the server.** The browser talks only to our origin, plus the Auth0 Universal Login pages.
166	- **Camera frames never leave the device.** MediaPipe runs in the browser via WASM, and the model and WASM are self-hosted ([Gesture recognition guide for Web](https://developers.google.com/edge/mediapipe/solutions/vision/gesture_recognizer/web_js)). Barcode decoding also runs locally. Only *still photos the user explicitly takes* for label or expiry reading go to Gemini, through our server.
167	- **Long-lived Node process.** Tiger's free services exclude connection pooling ([Tiger docs: create a service](https://www.tigerdata.com/docs/get-started/quickstart/create-service)). We hold one small postgres.js pool per process, which works on a VPS but would not suit serverless.
168	
169	### 3.2 Repository layout and ownership
170	
171	Owners: **P0** = Phase 0 (foundation, frozen after Phase 0), **A** = Cook Mode, **B** = Pantry & Nutrition, **C** = Recipes & Cooking Backend. See §18.
172	
173	```
174	/
175	├─ SPEC.md, CLAUDE.md, TASKS.md, .env.example            P0 (SPEC/CLAUDE edits by humans only)
176	├─ package.json, package-lock.json                       P0 (dependency changes: see §18.5)
177	├─ Dockerfile, docker-compose.yml, Caddyfile             P0 (C handles deploy tweaks in integration)
178	├─ next.config.ts (output: 'standalone', headers/CSP)    P0
179	├─ db/migrations/0001_init.sql, 0002_timescale.sql       P0 (changes: coordinated commit, §18.5)
180	├─ scripts/migrate.mjs                                   P0
181	├─ scripts/copy-assets.mjs (MediaPipe wasm + model, zxing wasm → public/)   P0
182	├─ public/mediapipe/wasm/*, public/models/gesture_recognizer.task           A
183	├─ public/zxing/*                                                            B
184	└─ src/
185	   ├─ proxy.ts                                           P0
186	   ├─ contracts/  domain.ts api.ts gesture.ts voice.ts index.ts fixtures/*   P0 (FROZEN)
187	   ├─ lib/        auth0.ts db.ts current-user.ts env.ts http.ts units.ts gtin.ts
188	   │              rate-limit.ts gemini/{client.ts,schemas.ts}                P0
189	   ├─ components/ui/**  (design tokens, Button, Card, Badge, Dialog, Toast) P0
190	   ├─ app/
191	   │   ├─ layout.tsx, globals.css, page.tsx (landing)    P0
192	   │   ├─ (app)/layout.tsx (auth gate + nav)             P0
193	   │   ├─ (app)/onboarding/**, (app)/settings/**         B
194	   │   ├─ (app)/today/**, (app)/pantry/**                B
195	   │   ├─ (app)/recipes/**                               C
196	   │   ├─ (app)/cook/[sessionId]/**                      A
197	   │   └─ api/
198	   │       ├─ me/route.ts                                B
199	   │       ├─ products/lookup/route.ts                   B

225	---
226	
227	## 4. Tech stack (pin exact versions)
228	
229	Pin every dependency to an **exact version** (no `^`/`~`) and commit the lockfile. Phase 0 runs `npm view <pkg> version` for each **[VERIFY]** row and writes the result into `package.json`.
230	
231	| Layer | Choice | Version (as of 2026-11-07) | Notes |
232	|---|---|---|---|
233	| Runtime | Node.js LTS | **22.x** (Docker `node:22-alpine`) | Auth0 SDK "requires Node.js 20 LTS and newer" ([nextjs-auth0 README](https://github.com/auth0/nextjs-auth0)) |
234	| Framework | `next` (App Router, TS, `output: 'standalone'`) | **16.4.5** ([npm registry, via @auth0/nextjs-auth0 research](https://registry.npmjs.org/@auth0/nextjs-auth0)) | Next 16 uses `proxy.ts` rather than `middleware.ts` for Auth0 ([Auth0 blog](https://auth0.com/blog/handling-auth-nextjs16-with-server-actions-middleware/)) |
235	| UI runtime | `react`, `react-dom` | whatever `next@16.4.5` peers require **[VERIFY]** | |
236	| Styling | Tailwind CSS (create-next-app default) | **[VERIFY]** | Design tokens in `globals.css` |
237	| Auth | `@auth0/nextjs-auth0` | **4.33.0** (published 2026-10-22) ([npm](https://registry.npmjs.org/@auth0/nextjs-auth0)) | Auth0 app type: Regular Web Application |
238	| DB driver | `postgres` (postgres.js) | **4.1.0** ([npm](https://registry.npmjs.org/postgres/latest)) | Hand-written SQL migrations. No ORM, because TimescaleDB DDL is raw SQL anyway |
239	| Validation | `zod` | 4.x **[VERIFY]** | Validate every request body and every LLM output |
240	| Gestures | `@mediapipe/tasks-vision` | **1.2.2** (published 2026-11-03) ([npm](https://registry.npmjs.org/@mediapipe/tasks-vision)) | Self-host WASM and model. Never use `@latest` URLs |
241	| Barcode | `barcode-detector` (Sec-ant, MIT, zxing-wasm) | 3.x exact **[VERIFY]** ([GitHub](https://github.com/Sec-ant/barcode-detector)) | Use `barcode-detector/ponyfill`. Self-host the `.wasm` |
242	| LLM | `@google/genai` | latest **[VERIFY]** | The legacy `@google/generative-ai` package is not used. Wrap all calls in `src/lib/gemini/` |
243	| Gemini model | `gemini-3.8-flash` (env `GEMINI_MODEL`) | listed as new; recommended for new projects ([Gemini models](https://aistudio.google.com/docs/models)) | `gemini-3.5-flash-lite` is the cheaper alternative. `gemini-2.0-flash` and `gemini-3-pro-preview` are **shut down** |
244	| Recipe parsing | `recipe-scrapers` (TS) | ≥1.10.0 **[VERIFY license/maintenance]** ([architecture doc](https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/recipe-scrapers@1.10.0/docs/architecture.md)) | Plus a hand-rolled JSON-LD fallback (§10.4) |
245	| TTS | ElevenLabs REST via `fetch` | model `eleven_flash_v2_5` ([Models](https://elevenlabs.io/docs/overview/models)) | No SDK needed. Its `play()` is server-only ([elevenlabs-js](https://github.com/elevenlabs/elevenlabs-js)) |
246	| Tests | `vitest` (unit), `@playwright/test` (one e2e smoke) | **[VERIFY]** | |
247	| Reverse proxy | Caddy | `caddy:2` image | Automatic HTTPS ([Vultr Caddy guide](https://docs.vultr.com/how-to-install-caddy-using-docker-on-a-vultr-cloud-server)) |
248	| Charts | Hand-rolled SVG (rings, 7-day bars) | none | Avoids a dependency |
249	
250	Do **not** add: an ORM, a state-management library (React context plus `useReducer` is enough), html5-qrcode or `@zxing/library` (both unmaintained per [Scanbot](https://scanbot.io/blog/popular-open-source-javascript-barcode-scanners/)), or the ElevenLabs JS SDK.
251	
252	---
253	
254	## 5. Data model (Tiger Data / TimescaleDB)
255	
256	### 5.1 Design rules
257	
258	- **Base units everywhere.** Store `quantity_base` in g, ml or count, and keep the user's `display_unit` alongside for display.
259	- **Nutrition per 100 g or 100 ml** is canonical. Per serving is derived, or stored when the source gives it.
260	- **Mutable state goes in plain tables:** `pantry_items`, `recipes`, `recipe_variants`, `cooking_sessions`.

# Mise: build spec for a hands-free pantry-to-plate cooking app

This SPEC.md specifies **Mise** (working name; rename freely), a Next.js web app built at HackCamp 2026 (nwPlus, UBC Vancouver, Nov 7–8, 2026). Users sign in with **Auth0**, add groceries by barcode, keep a per-user pantry with quantities and expiry dates in **Tiger Data** (TimescaleDB/Postgres), and get **real recipes found online by Gemini**, ranked toward whatever expires soonest. The original recipe is always shown first with attribution; an "AI-adapted" variant appears only when an ingredient is missing. Users cook hands-free with **MediaPipe** webcam gestures (scroll, next/previous step, timer, read aloud), with steps read aloud by **ElevenLabs** and `speechSynthesis` as the fallback. Finishing a recipe deducts what was used from the pantry and logs calories and protein in one database transaction. The app is served over HTTPS from a **Vultr** VPS, which the camera requires. The spec is written so three Claude Code accounts can build it in parallel through **Entire**. A Phase 0 foundation freezes the contracts in `src/contracts/`, the SQL schema and the stubs. After that, three workstreams (Cook Mode, Pantry & Nutrition, Recipes & Cooking Backend) each own separate directories, and an integration phase merges them. Researched facts are cited inline. Anything not confirmed against a primary source in research is marked **[VERIFY]**, and the open items are collected in §17. Treat those as the first things to check, not as settled.

---

## 0. How to use this document

- **Who reads this:** three Claude Code agents (one per teammate account) plus the humans steering them. Each agent reads §1–§8 (shared ground truth), its own workstream in §18, and the relevant feature sections in §9.
- **Source of truth order:** `src/contracts/**` (code) > this SPEC > comments. If the SPEC and the contracts disagree after Phase 0, the contracts win. Raise the mismatch with a human; don't silently diverge.
- **Markers:** **[VERIFY]** = not confirmed against a primary source during research; check before relying on it. **P0** = required for the demo, **P1** = should have, **P2** = stretch.
- Anthropic's guidance for specs like this: "The most useful specs are self-contained: they name the files and interfaces involved, state what is out of scope, and end with an end-to-end verification step." Keep CLAUDE.md short ([Claude Code best practices](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/best-practices.md)). This spec follows both.

---

## 1. Overview, goals and non-goals

### 1.1 Problem and pitch

Home cooks waste food they forgot they had, and following a recipe on a phone or laptop with wet, floury hands is awkward. Screens dim and you lose your place. Mise closes the loop: **scan groceries → know what expires → cook a real recipe that uses it → touch nothing while cooking → pantry and nutrition update themselves.** HackCamp's challenge is to "identify a problem facing a community and build a solution that makes a meaningful difference". Judging covers Problem & User Research, Innovation, Technical Implementation, Design & UX, and Presentation ([HackCamp 2026 Devpost](https://hackcamp-2026.devpost.com/)).

### 1.2 Goals (all confirmed by the team)

| # | Goal | Priority |
|---|---|---|
| G1 | Web app: Next.js App Router + TypeScript, deployed on Vultr over HTTPS | P0 |
| G2 | Auth0 login. Every pantry item, recipe, session and meal belongs to one user | P0 |
| G3 | Tiger Data (TimescaleDB/Postgres) as the only database | P0 |
| G4 | Add groceries by barcode, scanned with the camera or typed. Lookup chain: **dataandapis.com → Open Food Facts → Gemini reads a product/label photo → manual form** | P0 |
| G5 | Expiry date from a photo of the printed date (Gemini reads it, user confirms) or typed in | P0 |
| G6 | Pantry tracks quantities and expiry dates, and deducts ingredients after cooking | P0 |
| G7 | Gemini finds **real recipes online**, shown **original-first with source attribution**, ranked to prefer items closest to expiry | P0 |
| G8 | Only when an ingredient is missing, AI may propose an adaptation, clearly marked **"AI-adapted"** and kept separate from the original | P0 |
| G9 | MediaPipe hand gestures: scroll up/down, next/previous step, start/pause step timer, read step aloud | P0 |
| G10 | Read aloud with ElevenLabs, falling back to browser `speechSynthesis` | P0 |
| G11 | Nutrition per pantry item and per recipe serving. Strict, code-enforced diet/allergy filters. Daily calorie and protein tracking | P0 |
| G12 | Meals logged through a "Finish cooking" prompt (servings eaten) and through manual logging | P0 |
| G13 | Built by 3 Claude Code accounts collaborating through Entire (Sessions, Graph, Brain, Trails) | P0 |

### 1.3 Non-goals (explicitly out of scope)

- Native mobile apps. PWA install/offline mode is also out (the site should still work in mobile browsers).
- Writing recipes from scratch with AI. The AI only *finds* recipes and *adapts* them when ingredients are missing.
- Medical or dietetic advice, or certified allergen guarantees. The app filters strictly but tells users to check labels.
- Shopping lists, grocery ordering, price tracking, meal planning calendars.
- Sharing pantries between users or households, and any social features.
- Contributing products back to Open Food Facts, which would need an OFF account for writes ([OFF API intro](https://openfoodfacts.github.io/openfoodfacts-server/api/)).
- Voice *commands* (speech recognition) are P2 only. The P0 hands-free channel is gestures plus read-aloud.
- Moving gesture inference to a Web Worker (P2; see §11.7).
- Hosted vector search or "similar recipes" (P2).

### 1.4 Glossary

- **Original recipe:** the recipe exactly as parsed from the publisher's page (schema.org `Recipe`), with attribution. Never modified.
- **AI-adapted recipe:** a separate object that references an original and lists explicit substitutions for missing ingredients.
- **Base units:** grams (mass), millilitres (volume), `count` (pieces). Every stored quantity uses one of them.
- **GTIN:** the canonical 13-digit (or 14-digit) barcode key. UPC-A is left-padded with `0`.
- **FEFO:** first-expired-first-out, the rule for choosing which pantry row to deduct from.
- **Armed:** the gesture state in which commands are accepted. Users arm it by holding an open palm.

---

## 2. User flows

Each flow lists its happy path, then its branches. Feature IDs (F#) refer to §9.

### UF1: Sign in and onboarding (F1)
1. A visitor lands on `/`. The marketing hero has a "Sign in" button that links to `/auth/login` (Auth0 Universal Login).
2. After callback, the first authenticated request upserts a `users` row keyed by Auth0 `sub`.
3. If `onboarded_at` is null, redirect to `/onboarding`. There the user sets diets (vegetarian, vegan, gluten-free, dairy-free, high-protein), allergens, daily kcal and protein goals (optional), and time zone (default `America/Vancouver`).
4. The user lands on `/today`.

### UF2: Add a grocery by barcode (F2, F4, F5)
1. `/pantry/add` opens the camera scanner, with the **"Type barcode" input always visible**.
2. A code is accepted after 2 identical consecutive reads and a valid check digit. The client calls `POST /api/products/lookup`.
3. **Found** (cache, dataandapis or OFF): show a confirmation card with name, brand, image, nutrition per 100 g, package size, and source attribution ("Data: Open Food Facts, ODbL").
4. The user sets quantity (pre-filled from package size when known) and unit, then sets expiry: **"Photo of date"** (UF4) or **"Enter date"** or "No date".
5. Save. The item appears in `/pantry`, sorted by soonest expiry.
- **Branch, not found:** "We couldn't find this product." → **"Take photo of product & nutrition label"** (UF3) → if that fails or is declined → **manual form**. The manual form is reachable from every step.
- **Branch, provider down** (401/402/429/5xx/timeout): treated as a miss for the user, logged server-side. The flow continues to OFF, then to the photo step.

### UF3: Product from a label photo (F3)
1. The user captures 1–3 photos (front, nutrition panel, optional side). The client downscales them to about 1600 px on the long edge, JPEG q≈0.85.
2. `POST /api/vision/label` → Gemini returns a draft and the server runs sanity checks.
3. The manual form opens **pre-filled**. Flagged fields are highlighted. The user must press **Confirm** before anything is saved (`userVerified=true`).

### UF4: Expiry date from a photo (F4)
1. The user takes a close photo of the printed date.
2. `POST /api/vision/expiry` → the server assembles a date from Gemini's components and cross-checks it with a CFIA regex.
3. A date picker opens pre-filled, with the raw text shown ("Read: `BB/MA 2026 NO 15`"). If the order is ambiguous, the user picks from the candidates. **The user must confirm.** "Packaged on" dates are never accepted as expiry; instead the UI says "This looks like a packaged-on date".

### UF5: Find recipes (F6, F7, F10)
1. `/recipes` shows chips for expiring-soon items (≤ 3 days, pre-selected) and a "Find recipes" button. The user's diet/allergy filters appear as locked chips with a link to Settings.
2. `POST /api/recipes/search` streams progress ("Searching the web… / Reading 8 recipe pages… / Checking your allergies…"), then candidate cards arrive one by one.
3. Each card shows the title, the **source site and author**, coverage ("You have 7 of 9 ingredients"), the expiring items it uses (badge "uses spinach, expires in 2 days"), missing-ingredient count, ≈kcal and protein per serving, and total time.
4. Candidates that break a diet or allergy filter never appear. A collapsed "N recipes hidden by your filters" note lists them by reason (no recipe content shown).

### UF6: Recipe detail, original first, optional adaptation (F8, F9, F10)
1. `/recipes/[recipeId]` shows the **Original** card first: title, "From {siteName} by {author}", a "View original" link, ingredients exactly as published (each marked have / missing / staple), steps, and nutrition (our estimate with coverage, plus "Publisher's nutrition" if the page provided it).
2. If the recipe has missing ingredients, a secondary button reads **"Suggest an AI adaptation using my pantry"**. Pressing it calls `POST /api/recipes/[id]/adapt`. The result appears in a **separate card with an "AI-adapted" badge** on a different background. It lists substitutions ("Missing: buttermilk → Using: Greek yogurt + lemon (from your pantry)"), changed steps, warnings, and re-estimated nutrition.
3. "Cook original" and "Cook AI-adapted" (when present) are separate buttons, each with a servings stepper.

### UF7: Cook hands-free (F11, F12, F13)
1. "Cook" → `POST /api/cook/sessions` → `/cook/[sessionId]`. The **"Start cooking" tap** unlocks audio and requests a screen wake lock.
2. One step per screen, in large type. The step's ingredients and quantities are listed and timer chips are docked at the bottom.
3. A **"Hands-free" toggle** loads MediaPipe lazily, asks for camera permission, and shows the HUD with a gesture legend. Open palm (hold) arms the system. Then swipe = next/previous, thumb up/down (hold) = scroll, fist (hold) = timer start/pause, victory sign (hold) = read step aloud / stop.
4. Each control also has big tap targets and keyboard shortcuts.
5. Refreshing or reopening the page offers "Resume at step 5?". Timers continue correctly because they are stored as absolute end times.

### UF8: Finish cooking (F14)
1. On the last step (or any time from the menu) → **"Finish cooking"** dialog.
2. The dialog shows **Servings cooked** (default = planned), **Servings you ate** (default 1; 0 allowed), and a **deduction preview** with one line per matched pantry item ("Spinach: 150 g of 200 g → 50 g left"). Lines are editable and can be unchecked. Lines the app couldn't convert are flagged "Adjust manually". The nutrition for the servings eaten is editable.
3. Confirm → one transaction deducts the pantry, writes pantry events, inserts the meal log and closes the session → navigate to `/today` with a toast ("Logged 1 serving · 540 kcal · 32 g protein").

### UF9: Daily tracking and manual logging (F15)
1. `/today` shows kcal and protein rings against the goals, today's meals list, a 7-day bar chart, and "Expiring soon" pantry items.
2. **"Log food"** offers three tabs: *From pantry* (pick item + amount; "Also remove from pantry" checkbox, default on), *Scan* (barcode → product → amount), *Quick add* (label + kcal + protein).
3. The user can delete a meal from today's list.

---

## 3. Architecture

### 3.1 System diagram

```
                         ┌──────────────────────── Browser (HTTPS secure context) ─────────────────────────┐
                         │  Next.js client components                                                        │
                         │  ┌──────────────┐  ┌───────────────────┐  ┌──────────────┐  ┌──────────────────┐ │
                         │  │ Scanner       │  │ Cook mode UI      │  │ Voice player │  │ Today / Pantry / │ │
                         │  │ BarcodeDetector│  │ steps, timers,    │  │ <audio> +    │  │ Recipes pages    │ │
                         │  │ (native or    │  │ wake lock, resume │  │ speechSynth  │  │                  │ │
                         │  │ zxing-wasm)   │  │ (localStorage)    │  │ fallback     │  │                  │ │
                         │  └──────┬───────┘  └───────┬───────────┘  └──────┬───────┘  └────────┬─────────┘ │
                         │         │      ┌───────────┴────────────┐        │                   │           │
                         │         │      │ GestureController      │        │                   │           │
                         │         │      │ MediaPipe tasks-vision │  camera frames NEVER leave the device  │
                         │         │      │ (WASM, self-hosted)    │        │                   │           │
                         │         │      └────────────────────────┘        │                   │           │
                         └─────────┼────────────────────┼───────────────────┼───────────────────┼───────────┘
                                   │ fetch (JSON / multipart / NDJSON / audio)                    │
┌──────────────────────────────────▼────────────────────▼───────────────────▼───────────────────▼───────────┐
│ Vultr VPS (Ubuntu, Docker)                                                                                │
│  Caddy 2 (TLS via Let's Encrypt, :80/:443)  ──reverse_proxy──►  Next.js standalone (Node 22) :3000        │
│                                                                  ├─ src/proxy.ts → auth0.middleware()     │
│                                                                  ├─ /auth/* (Auth0 SDK routes)            │
│                                                                  ├─ /api/* route handlers (Node runtime)  │
│                                                                  │    requireUser() on every handler      │
│                                                                  └─ src/server/** domain logic            │
└───────┬───────────────┬──────────────────┬──────────────────┬──────────────────┬──────────────┬──────────┘
        │               │                  │                  │                  │              │
        ▼               ▼                  ▼                  ▼                  ▼              ▼
   Auth0 tenant   Tiger Cloud        dataandapis.com     Open Food Facts     Gemini API     ElevenLabs
   (Universal     (Postgres +        Barcode Lookup      v2 product API      (grounded      TTS stream
    Login)        TimescaleDB,       (X-Api-Key)         (custom UA)         search, vision, (xi-api-key)
                  us-east-1)                                                  JSON output)
                                                                                   │
                                                                                   ▼
                                                                        Publisher recipe pages
                                                                        (server-side fetch →
                                                                         schema.org Recipe JSON-LD)
```

Key properties:
- **All third-party keys live on the server.** The browser talks only to our origin, plus the Auth0 Universal Login pages.
- **Camera frames never leave the device.** MediaPipe runs in the browser via WASM, and the model and WASM are self-hosted ([Gesture recognition guide for Web](https://developers.google.com/edge/mediapipe/solutions/vision/gesture_recognizer/web_js)). Barcode decoding also runs locally. Only *still photos the user explicitly takes* for label or expiry reading go to Gemini, through our server.
- **Long-lived Node process.** Tiger's free services exclude connection pooling ([Tiger docs: create a service](https://www.tigerdata.com/docs/get-started/quickstart/create-service)). We hold one small postgres.js pool per process, which works on a VPS but would not suit serverless.

### 3.2 Repository layout and ownership

Owners: **P0** = Phase 0 (foundation, frozen after Phase 0), **A** = Cook Mode, **B** = Pantry & Nutrition, **C** = Recipes & Cooking Backend. See §18.

```

---

## 4. Tech stack (pin exact versions)

Pin every dependency to an **exact version** (no `^`/`~`) and commit the lockfile. Phase 0 runs `npm view <pkg> version` for each **[VERIFY]** row and writes the result into `package.json`.

| Layer | Choice | Version (as of 2026-11-07) | Notes |

## 5. Data model (Tiger Data / TimescaleDB)

### 5.1 Design rules

- **Base units everywhere.** Store `quantity_base` in g, ml or count, and keep the user's `display_unit` alongside for display.
- **Nutrition per 100 g or 100 ml** is canonical. Per serving is derived, or stored when the source gives it.
- **Mutable state goes in plain tables:** `pantry_items`, `recipes`, `recipe_variants`, `cooking_sessions`.

1535	### 10.5 ElevenLabs text-to-speech
1536	
1537	- **Request:** `POST https://api.elevenlabs.io/v1/text-to-speech/{voice_id}/stream?output_format=mp3_44100_128`
1538	  - Header `xi-api-key`.
1539	  - Body `{ text, model_id: "eleven_flash_v2_5" }`. The API default model is `eleven_multilingual_v2`, so **always set the model explicitly**.
1540	  - `optimize_streaming_latency` is deprecated.
1541	  - Source: [Stream speech](https://elevenlabs.io/docs/api-reference/text-to-speech/stream)
1542	- **Why HTTP streaming:** it is the recommended mode "for cases where the input text is available up-front", which fits recipe steps. WebSockets are for incremental LLM text ([latency guide](https://elevenlabs.io/docs/eleven-api/guides/how-to/best-practices/latency-optimization.md)).
1543	- **Model choice:** Flash v2.5 has about 100 ms median model latency, up to 40,000 characters per request, 32 languages, and 50% lower per-character price. `eleven_turbo_v2_5` is deprecated ([Models](https://elevenlabs.io/docs/overview/models)).
1544	- **Cost:** Flash/Turbo API pricing is **$0.04 per 1K characters** ([API pricing](https://elevenlabs.io/pricing/api)). A 15-step recipe at about 150 characters per step comes to roughly $0.09, and caching makes repeat demos close to free.
1545	- **Route** (`app/api/tts/route.ts`):
1546	  1. Validate 1–2000 chars.
1547	  2. If there is no key, return 503 `UPSTREAM_UNAVAILABLE`.
1548	  3. Stream `r.body` through with `Content-Type: audio/mpeg` and `Cache-Control: private, max-age=86400`.
1549	  4. If the upstream response is non-2xx, return 502, and the client falls back.

1551	### 10.6 MediaPipe Tasks Vision
1552	
1553	- **Package and assets:** `@mediapipe/tasks-vision@1.2.2`. It ships two WASM variants of about 14.6 MB each, and types `FilesetResolver.forVisionTasks(basePath?, useModule?)`, `BaseOptions.delegate: "CPU" | "GPU"` and `recognizeForVideo(frame, timestamp)`, which is synchronous ([npm tarball](https://registry.npmjs.org/@mediapipe/tasks-vision)).
1554	- **Model file:** the canonical model URL is `https://storage.googleapis.com/mediapipe-models/gesture_recognizer/gesture_recognizer/float16/latest/gesture_recognizer.task` ([overview](https://developers.google.com/edge/mediapipe/solutions/vision/gesture_recognizer)). Download it once, commit it to `public/models/`, and **[VERIFY]** that the URL serves (research couldn't reach it through the sandbox proxy).
1555	- **Self-hosting:** `scripts/copy-assets.mjs` (postinstall) copies `node_modules/@mediapipe/tasks-vision/wasm/*` → `public/mediapipe/wasm/`. Never use the `@latest` CDN path. The package shipped four minor releases in Oct–Nov 2026.
1556	- **Canned gestures:** None, Closed_Fist, Open_Palm, Pointing_Up, Thumb_Down, Thumb_Up, Victory, ILoveYou. **Handedness is reported for the subject's hand, and a mirrored image inverts it** ([overview](https://developers.google.com/edge/mediapipe/solutions/vision/gesture_recognizer)).
1557	- **Threading:** `recognizeForVideo()` blocks the UI thread, and Google recommends web workers for camera input ([web guide](https://developers.google.com/edge/mediapipe/solutions/vision/gesture_recognizer/web_js)). We start on the main thread behind `GestureSource` (§11.7).
1558	- **Performance:** the only published benchmarks are for a Pixel 6: GestureRecognizer averages about 16.8 ms on CPU and 20.9 ms on GPU. Laptop numbers are unknown, so ship a dev FPS counter.

1582	## 11. Gesture state machine (owned by A)
1583	
1584	No published thresholds exist for kitchen gesture control. Every number below is an **engineering starting value to tune**, exposed in `GestureConfig` and adjustable in Settings ("Sensitivity", "Hold time", "Swipe direction", "Always armed").
1585	
1586	### 11.1 Mapping
1587	
1588	| User control (confirmed) | Gesture | Fires | Why |
1589	|---|---|---|---|
1590	| *(prerequisite)* Arm | `Open_Palm` held ≥ **600 ms** | `ARM`, armed for **5 s**. The window extends after each action | Stirring, chopping and reaching never fire commands |
1591	| Next / previous step | **Horizontal swipe** while armed | `NEXT_STEP` / `PREV_STEP` | Natural page turn. Default: hand moves **right→left = next** (phone-carousel convention), configurable |
1592	| Scroll up / down | `Thumb_Up` / `Thumb_Down` held | First tick at **600 ms**, then every **700 ms** while held, each scrolling **40% of the viewport** | Avoids up/down swipes, which collide with stirring and reaching |
1593	| Start / pause step timer | `Closed_Fist` held ≥ **800 ms**, score ≥ **0.8** | `TIMER_TOGGLE` (once per hold) | Distinct pose. A long hold and high score guard against a fist around a spoon handle |
1594	| Read step aloud / stop | `Victory` held ≥ **800 ms** | `SPEAK_TOGGLE` (once per hold) | Rare in kitchen motion and easier to form than ILoveYou |
1595	
1596	Recognizer options:
1597	- `runningMode: 'VIDEO'`, `numHands: 1`.
1598	- `cannedGesturesClassifierOptions: { scoreThreshold: 0.6, categoryAllowlist: ['Open_Palm','Closed_Fist','Thumb_Up','Thumb_Down','Victory'] }`. The option comes from the [1.2.2 types](https://registry.npmjs.org/@mediapipe/tasks-vision).
1599	- The engine applies `minScore = 0.7` (and 0.8 for the fist).
1600	
1601	### 11.2 States and transitions
1602	
1603	```
1604	 off ──toggle on──► loading ──model+camera ok──► no_hand
1605	  ▲                   │ └─permission denied──► permission_needed ──retry──► loading
1606	  │                   └─model/wasm fail──► error (buttons/keyboard still work)
1607	  └─toggle off / page hide / route leave (stop tracks, close recognizer)
1608	
1609	 no_hand ──hand detected (bbox h ≥ 8% frame, not touching edge)──► hand_seen
1610	 hand_seen ──no hand ≥ 300 ms──► no_hand
1611	 hand_seen ──Open_Palm held ≥ armHoldMs──► armed   (emit ARM; armedUntil = now + 5000)
1612	 armed ──pose P ∈ {Closed_Fist, Victory, Thumb_Up, Thumb_Down} starts──► holding(P)
1613	 holding(P) ──P held ≥ threshold──► emit action ──► cooldown   (scroll: repeat tick, stays holding)
1614	 holding(P) ──P changes / hand lost before threshold──► armed
1615	 armed ──swipe detected──► emit NEXT/PREV ──► cooldown
1616	 cooldown ──cooldownMs elapsed AND released (pose changed or no hand ≥ 300 ms)──► armed
1617	 armed ──now > armedUntil──► hand_seen / no_hand   (emit DISARM)
1618	 any ──alwaysArmed=true──► arming step skipped
1619	```
1620	
1621	Rules:
1622	- **Release-to-rearm:** a discrete pose action fires at most once per continuous hold.
1623	- **Global cooldown:** 1200 ms after any discrete action (swipe, timer, speak). Scroll ticks don't trigger it, but a release after scrolling adds a 300 ms cooldown.
1624	- **Successful actions extend the armed window** by another 5 s from the action time.
1625	
1626	### 11.3 Swipe detection
1627	
1628	- Palm centre = mean of landmarks **0, 5, 9, 13, 17**. Smooth with an EMA (α = 0.5) before computing velocity.
1629	- Mirror x so directions match what the user sees: `x' = 1 − x`. **Never use the handedness label for direction.**
1630	- Keep a ring buffer of `{t, x, y}` over the last **400 ms**.
1631	- Fire when **all** of these hold:
1632	  - `|Δx| ≥ 0.25` of frame width
1633	  - `|Δx| ≥ 2·|Δy|`
1634	  - peak velocity ≥ **1.0 frame-widths/s**
1635	  - the pose was not `Closed_Fist` for most of the window
1636	- After firing, clear the buffer. The 1200 ms cooldown also swallows the return stroke.
1637	
1638	### 11.4 Constants (`features/gesture/config.ts`)
1639	
1640	```ts
1641	export const DEFAULT_GESTURE_CONFIG: GestureConfig = {
1642	  minScore: 0.7, fistMinScore: 0.8, classifierScoreThreshold: 0.6,
1643	  armHoldMs: 600, actionHoldMs: 800, armWindowMs: 5000, alwaysArmed: false,
1644	  cooldownMs: 1200, releaseMs: 300,
1645	  scrollFirstMs: 600, scrollRepeatMs: 700, scrollFraction: 0.4,
1646	  swipeWindowMs: 400, swipeMinDx: 0.25, swipeDxToDyRatio: 2, swipeMinVelocity: 1.0,
1647	  swipeNextDirection: 'left',
1648	  minHandHeightFrac: 0.08, targetFps: 15, idleFps: 5, idleAfterMs: 10_000,
1649	  delegate: 'GPU',
1650	};
1651	```
1652	
1653	### 11.5 Runtime loop (main thread, `features/gesture/MediaPipeGestureSource.ts`)
1654	
1655	- **Loading:** `GestureController` is a `'use client'` component loaded with `next/dynamic(..., { ssr: false })` from **another client component**. `ssr:false` is not supported in Server Components ([Next.js lazy loading](https://nextjs.org/docs/app/guides/lazy-loading)).
1656	- **Init:** `forVisionTasks('/mediapipe/wasm')`, then `GestureRecognizer.createFromOptions(...)` with `delegate: 'GPU'`, catching failure and retrying with `'CPU'`. Make the delegate configurable, because GPU was *slower* than CPU on the Pixel 6 benchmark.
1657	- **Camera:** `getUserMedia({ video: { facingMode: 'user', width: {ideal: 640}, height: {ideal: 480}, frameRate: {ideal: 30} }, audio: false })`. Map `NotAllowedError`, `NotFoundError` and `NotReadableError`, and handle `navigator.mediaDevices === undefined` (insecure context). A prompt the user ignores may never settle, so show "Waiting for camera permission…" ([MDN getUserMedia](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/MediaDevices/getUserMedia)).
1658	- **Frame loop:** a rAF loop that processes a frame only when `video.readyState >= 2 && video.currentTime !== last`, throttled to `targetFps`. Drop to `idleFps` after `idleAfterMs` with no hand. Pass a monotonic `performance.now()` timestamp ([HandLandmarker web guide](https://developers.google.com/edge/mediapipe/solutions/vision/hand_landmarker/web_js)).
1659	- **Strict Mode:** React runs an extra setup and cleanup cycle in dev ([React StrictMode](https://react.dev/reference/react/StrictMode)), so use an `aborted` flag and full cleanup: `cancelAnimationFrame`, stop the tracks, `recognizer.close()`.
1660	- **Visibility:** pause on `visibilitychange` (hidden).
1661	- **State placement:** keep the recognizer, stream and engine in refs. Push HUD state to React at ≤ 10 Hz.
1662	
1663	### 11.6 HUD
1664	
1665	- **Placement:** a corner widget, ≤ 20% of the screen.
1666	- **Contents:**
1667	  - Optional mirrored camera thumbnail (toggle; off hides the video element but keeps inference running).
1668	  - State chip: "Show your palm to start" → "Ready · 4 s" → "Hold fist… ◔" → "Timer started ✓".
1669	  - Radial hold-progress ring.
1670	  - Gesture legend (5 icons).
1671	  - Hints: "Move closer" (hand bbox < 8%), "Turn on a light" (low confidence for 3 s), "One hand please".
1672	- **Debug:** landmarks are drawn only when `NEXT_PUBLIC_GESTURE_DEBUG=true`.
1673	- **Feedback:** every fired action produces a brief full-screen edge flash plus a soft click sound (respecting reduced motion) and an `aria-live` announcement, because the cook is often looking at the pan rather than the screen.
1674	- **Camera indicator:** a persistent "Camera on" pill with a one-tap off switch.
1675	
1676	### 11.7 Worker offload (P2)
1677	
1678	The `GestureSource` interface allows a `WorkerGestureSource`:
1679	- The main thread posts transferable `VideoFrame`/`ImageBitmap` objects, with one frame in flight.
1680	- The worker is created with `new Worker(new URL('./gesture.worker.ts', import.meta.url), { type: 'module' })` and initialized with `forVisionTasks(base, true)`.
1681	- Fishjam used this pattern in production ([Fishjam blog](https://fishjam.swmansion.com/blog/real-time-gesture-recognition-in-videoconferencing-4711855a1a53)).
1682	- Module workers have a history of `importScripts` breakage, and a maintainer said 0.10.35 "should work" ([issue #5257](https://github.com/google-ai-edge/mediapipe/issues/5257)). `DrawingUtils` fails in workers. Test on Safari before switching.
1683	
1684	### 11.8 Testability
1685	
1686	- `GestureEngine` is a pure class: `update(result: GestureRecognizerResult-like, now: number)`. It takes no DOM or MediaPipe imports, so Vitest can drive it with synthetic landmark sequences in `features/gesture/__fixtures__/`.
1687	- `KeyboardGestureSource` (Phase 0 mock) maps keys to `GestureAction`s so Cook Mode can be built before MediaPipe works.

1691	## 12. UX rules (apply everywhere)
1692	
1693	1. **Original before AI, always.** Anything Gemini *generated or transformed* carries a visible badge: "AI-adapted" on adaptations, "Read by AI, please confirm" on label and expiry drafts, "≈ estimate" on computed nutrition. Publisher content carries attribution instead.
1694	2. **Confirm before save** for every AI extraction. Nothing from Gemini reaches the database without a user tap.
1695	3. **Every gesture has a tap and a keyboard equivalent.** Gestures are never the only path, and hands-free is opt-in per session.
1696	4. **Kitchen-distance readability in cook mode:**
1697	   - Step text ≥ 32 px.
1698	   - One step per screen.
1699	   - Tap targets ≥ 25% of width for Prev and Next, and ≥ 56 px elsewhere.
1700	   - Contrast ≥ WCAG AA. Dark theme default in cook mode.
1701	5. **Colour is never the only signal.** Expiry bands also show text ("2 days"), and have/missing markers use icon + label.
1702	6. **Feedback for hands-free actions** goes through three channels: visual flash, sound, and `aria-live` text. Respect `prefers-reduced-motion`.
1703	7. **Progressive results.** Recipe search streams status messages and cards. Never show a spinner with no message for more than 2 s.
1704	8. **Honest empty and error states:**
1705	   - "We couldn't find this product" leads straight to the next fallback.
1706	   - "Camera blocked" offers buttons and keyboard.
1707	   - "Voice: Device" appears when ElevenLabs is unavailable.
1708	9. **"Best before", not "Expires"**, unless Gemini classified the date as `expiry`/`use_by`. Show the raw printed text next to the parsed date.
1709	10. **Allergy copy:** filters are strict, but the app always says "Always check product labels for allergens." Never claim a recipe is "safe".
1710	11. **Units:** show the user's display unit and accept common abbreviations. Never show raw base units to users.
1711	12. **Design deliverable:** produce a Figma file of the main screens (Today, Pantry, Scan, Recipes, Recipe detail with Original + AI-adapted, Cook mode + HUD) for the Best Design submission (§16).

1715	## 13. Security and privacy
1716	
1717	| Area | Rule |
1718	|---|---|
1719	| Secrets | Server-only. None use the `NEXT_PUBLIC_` prefix. `.env.production` lives on the VPS with `chmod 600` and is never baked into the image. Entire's secrets redaction is a bonus, not a control |
1720	| AuthZ | `requireUser()` in every route handler and Server Action. Every SQL statement includes `user_id = ${user.id}`. IDs in URLs are always re-checked against the user, and a mismatch returns **404** (not 403) |
1721	| Input validation | Zod on every body and query. Barcode digits 8–14. Text caps (TTS 2000, freeText 100). Image MIME allowlist and ≤ 4 MB each, ≤ 3 per request |
1722	| LLM output | Treated as untrusted input: Zod-validated, values sanity-checked, pantry IDs verified, allergens re-checked in code, URLs verified by fetch |
1723	| SSRF (recipe fetcher) | `server/recipes/safe-fetch.ts`: only `http(s)` on ports 80/443. Resolve DNS and **reject private, loopback, link-local and metadata IPs** (10/8, 172.16/12, 192.168/16, 127/8, 169.254/16, ::1, fc00::/7), re-checked on every redirect. Max 5 redirects, 5 s timeout, 2 MB body cap, `text/html` only |
1724	| Rendering third-party HTML | Never `dangerouslySetInnerHTML` publisher HTML. Parse it to text. Gemini's Search Suggestions HTML is rendered **unmodified inside a sandboxed `<iframe srcdoc>`** (`sandbox="allow-popups allow-popups-to-escape-sandbox"`) **[VERIFY this satisfies the Grounding display terms]** |
1725	| Camera and video | Frames are processed locally and never recorded, uploaded or stored. Model and WASM are self-hosted, so there are no third-party requests while hands-free is on. The camera starts only after an explicit toggle, a persistent indicator is shown, and tracks stop on toggle-off, page hide and route leave |
1726	| Photos | Label and expiry photos go to Gemini through our server for one request and are **not persisted** (memory only). The UI copy says so |
1727	| Headers | `Permissions-Policy: camera=(self), microphone=()`, `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff`, `Referrer-Policy: strict-origin-when-cross-origin`, `frame-ancestors 'none'`. CSP (P1): `script-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline' 'wasm-unsafe-eval'`; `img-src 'self' data: blob: https:`; `media-src 'self' blob:`; `connect-src 'self'`; `worker-src 'self' blob:`. The `'wasm-unsafe-eval'` source is needed for Emscripten WASM (general knowledge **[VERIFY]**) |
1728	| Abuse and cost | Per-user rate limits (§7). TTS text cap. Discovery cache. Barcode cache and single-flight |
1729	| Licensing and attribution | "Product data © Open Food Facts contributors, ODbL" in the footer and on product cards. OFF images are CC BY-SA. Recipe attribution and "View original" on every recipe |
1730	| Data deletion | Settings → "Delete my data" deletes the `users` row (cascades) (P1) |

2082	## Conclusion
2083	
2084	The riskiest parts of this build aren't gestures or auth. They are three LLM boundaries: finding real URLs, reading labels and dates, and adapting recipes. In each one, Gemini's output can be well-formed and still wrong. The spec therefore keeps Gemini out of every decision that has to be correct. Gemini finds candidate URLs, but the recipe content shown is whatever the publisher's own markup says, fetched and parsed by our code. Gemini reads a label, but a person confirms it. Gemini proposes a substitution, and `checkDiet` decides whether it is allowed. That split is also what lets three agents work in parallel safely, because the deterministic modules (units, GTIN, diet, scoring, timers, the gesture engine) are pure and testable against frozen contracts with no network. The two choices most worth revisiting after the event are the gesture thresholds in §11.4, which no published study validates, and how much publisher step text to store. That second one is a product and legal call, and the research could only partly settle it.

### 10.5 ElevenLabs text-to-speech

- **Request:** `POST https://api.elevenlabs.io/v1/text-to-speech/{voice_id}/stream?output_format=mp3_44100_128`
  - Header `xi-api-key`.
  - Body `{ text, model_id: "eleven_flash_v2_5" }`. The API default model is `eleven_multilingual_v2`, so **always set the model explicitly**.
  - `optimize_streaming_latency` is deprecated.
  - Source: [Stream speech](https://elevenlabs.io/docs/api-reference/text-to-speech/stream)
- **Why HTTP streaming:** it is the recommended mode "for cases where the input text is available up-front", which fits recipe steps. WebSockets are for incremental LLM text ([latency guide](https://elevenlabs.io/docs/eleven-api/guides/how-to/best-practices/latency-optimization.md)).
- **Model choice:** Flash v2.5 has about 100 ms median model latency, up to 40,000 characters per request, 32 languages, and 50% lower per-character price. `eleven_turbo_v2_5` is deprecated ([Models](https://elevenlabs.io/docs/overview/models)).
- **Cost:** Flash/Turbo API pricing is **$0.04 per 1K characters** ([API pricing](https://elevenlabs.io/pricing/api)). A 15-step recipe at about 150 characters per step comes to roughly $0.09, and caching makes repeat demos close to free.
- **Route** (`app/api/tts/route.ts`):
  1. Validate 1–2000 chars.
  2. If there is no key, return 503 `UPSTREAM_UNAVAILABLE`.
  3. Stream `r.body` through with `Content-Type: audio/mpeg` and `Cache-Control: private, max-age=86400`.
  4. If the upstream response is non-2xx, return 502, and the client falls back.

### 10.6 MediaPipe Tasks Vision

- **Package and assets:** `@mediapipe/tasks-vision@1.2.2`. It ships two WASM variants of about 14.6 MB each, and types `FilesetResolver.forVisionTasks(basePath?, useModule?)`, `BaseOptions.delegate: "CPU" | "GPU"` and `recognizeForVideo(frame, timestamp)`, which is synchronous ([npm tarball](https://registry.npmjs.org/@mediapipe/tasks-vision)).
- **Model file:** the canonical model URL is `https://storage.googleapis.com/mediapipe-models/gesture_recognizer/gesture_recognizer/float16/latest/gesture_recognizer.task` ([overview](https://developers.google.com/edge/mediapipe/solutions/vision/gesture_recognizer)). Download it once, commit it to `public/models/`, and **[VERIFY]** that the URL serves (research couldn't reach it through the sandbox proxy).
- **Self-hosting:** `scripts/copy-assets.mjs` (postinstall) copies `node_modules/@mediapipe/tasks-vision/wasm/*` → `public/mediapipe/wasm/`. Never use the `@latest` CDN path. The package shipped four minor releases in Oct–Nov 2026.
- **Canned gestures:** None, Closed_Fist, Open_Palm, Pointing_Up, Thumb_Down, Thumb_Up, Victory, ILoveYou. **Handedness is reported for the subject's hand, and a mirrored image inverts it** ([overview](https://developers.google.com/edge/mediapipe/solutions/vision/gesture_recognizer)).
- **Threading:** `recognizeForVideo()` blocks the UI thread, and Google recommends web workers for camera input ([web guide](https://developers.google.com/edge/mediapipe/solutions/vision/gesture_recognizer/web_js)). We start on the main thread behind `GestureSource` (§11.7).
- **Performance:** the only published benchmarks are for a Pixel 6: GestureRecognizer averages about 16.8 ms on CPU and 20.9 ms on GPU. Laptop numbers are unknown, so ship a dev FPS counter.

## 11. Gesture state machine (owned by A)

No published thresholds exist for kitchen gesture control. Every number below is an **engineering starting value to tune**, exposed in `GestureConfig` and adjustable in Settings ("Sensitivity", "Hold time", "Swipe direction", "Always armed").

### 11.1 Mapping

| User control (confirmed) | Gesture | Fires | Why |
|---|---|---|---|
| *(prerequisite)* Arm | `Open_Palm` held ≥ **600 ms** | `ARM`, armed for **5 s**. The window extends after each action | Stirring, chopping and reaching never fire commands |
| Next / previous step | **Horizontal swipe** while armed | `NEXT_STEP` / `PREV_STEP` | Natural page turn. Default: hand moves **right→left = next** (phone-carousel convention), configurable |
| Scroll up / down | `Thumb_Up` / `Thumb_Down` held | First tick at **600 ms**, then every **700 ms** while held, each scrolling **40% of the viewport** | Avoids up/down swipes, which collide with stirring and reaching |
| Start / pause step timer | `Closed_Fist` held ≥ **800 ms**, score ≥ **0.8** | `TIMER_TOGGLE` (once per hold) | Distinct pose. A long hold and high score guard against a fist around a spoon handle |
| Read step aloud / stop | `Victory` held ≥ **800 ms** | `SPEAK_TOGGLE` (once per hold) | Rare in kitchen motion and easier to form than ILoveYou |

Recognizer options:
- `runningMode: 'VIDEO'`, `numHands: 1`.
- `cannedGesturesClassifierOptions: { scoreThreshold: 0.6, categoryAllowlist: ['Open_Palm','Closed_Fist','Thumb_Up','Thumb_Down','Victory'] }`. The option comes from the [1.2.2 types](https://registry.npmjs.org/@mediapipe/tasks-vision).
- The engine applies `minScore = 0.7` (and 0.8 for the fist).

### 11.2 States and transitions

```
 off ──toggle on──► loading ──model+camera ok──► no_hand
  ▲                   │ └─permission denied──► permission_needed ──retry──► loading
  │                   └─model/wasm fail──► error (buttons/keyboard still work)
  └─toggle off / page hide / route leave (stop tracks, close recognizer)

 no_hand ──hand detected (bbox h ≥ 8% frame, not touching edge)──► hand_seen
 hand_seen ──no hand ≥ 300 ms──► no_hand
 hand_seen ──Open_Palm held ≥ armHoldMs──► armed   (emit ARM; armedUntil = now + 5000)
 armed ──pose P ∈ {Closed_Fist, Victory, Thumb_Up, Thumb_Down} starts──► holding(P)
 holding(P) ──P held ≥ threshold──► emit action ──► cooldown   (scroll: repeat tick, stays holding)
 holding(P) ──P changes / hand lost before threshold──► armed
 armed ──swipe detected──► emit NEXT/PREV ──► cooldown
 cooldown ──cooldownMs elapsed AND released (pose changed or no hand ≥ 300 ms)──► armed
 armed ──now > armedUntil──► hand_seen / no_hand   (emit DISARM)
 any ──alwaysArmed=true──► arming step skipped
```

Rules:
- **Release-to-rearm:** a discrete pose action fires at most once per continuous hold.
- **Global cooldown:** 1200 ms after any discrete action (swipe, timer, speak). Scroll ticks don't trigger it, but a release after scrolling adds a 300 ms cooldown.
- **Successful actions extend the armed window** by another 5 s from the action time.

### 11.3 Swipe detection

- Palm centre = mean of landmarks **0, 5, 9, 13, 17**. Smooth with an EMA (α = 0.5) before computing velocity.
- Mirror x so directions match what the user sees: `x' = 1 − x`. **Never use the handedness label for direction.**
- Keep a ring buffer of `{t, x, y}` over the last **400 ms**.
- Fire when **all** of these hold:
  - `|Δx| ≥ 0.25` of frame width
  - `|Δx| ≥ 2·|Δy|`
  - peak velocity ≥ **1.0 frame-widths/s**
  - the pose was not `Closed_Fist` for most of the window
- After firing, clear the buffer. The 1200 ms cooldown also swallows the return stroke.

### 11.4 Constants (`features/gesture/config.ts`)

```ts
export const DEFAULT_GESTURE_CONFIG: GestureConfig = {
  minScore: 0.7, fistMinScore: 0.8, classifierScoreThreshold: 0.6,
  armHoldMs: 600, actionHoldMs: 800, armWindowMs: 5000, alwaysArmed: false,
  cooldownMs: 1200, releaseMs: 300,
  scrollFirstMs: 600, scrollRepeatMs: 700, scrollFraction: 0.4,
  swipeWindowMs: 400, swipeMinDx: 0.25, swipeDxToDyRatio: 2, swipeMinVelocity: 1.0,
  swipeNextDirection: 'left',
  minHandHeightFrac: 0.08, targetFps: 15, idleFps: 5, idleAfterMs: 10_000,
  delegate: 'GPU',
};
```

### 11.5 Runtime loop (main thread, `features/gesture/MediaPipeGestureSource.ts`)

- **Loading:** `GestureController` is a `'use client'` component loaded with `next/dynamic(..., { ssr: false })` from **another client component**. `ssr:false` is not supported in Server Components ([Next.js lazy loading](https://nextjs.org/docs/app/guides/lazy-loading)).
- **Init:** `forVisionTasks('/mediapipe/wasm')`, then `GestureRecognizer.createFromOptions(...)` with `delegate: 'GPU'`, catching failure and retrying with `'CPU'`. Make the delegate configurable, because GPU was *slower* than CPU on the Pixel 6 benchmark.
- **Camera:** `getUserMedia({ video: { facingMode: 'user', width: {ideal: 640}, height: {ideal: 480}, frameRate: {ideal: 30} }, audio: false })`. Map `NotAllowedError`, `NotFoundError` and `NotReadableError`, and handle `navigator.mediaDevices === undefined` (insecure context). A prompt the user ignores may never settle, so show "Waiting for camera permission…" ([MDN getUserMedia](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/MediaDevices/getUserMedia)).
- **Frame loop:** a rAF loop that processes a frame only when `video.readyState >= 2 && video.currentTime !== last`, throttled to `targetFps`. Drop to `idleFps` after `idleAfterMs` with no hand. Pass a monotonic `performance.now()` timestamp ([HandLandmarker web guide](https://developers.google.com/edge/mediapipe/solutions/vision/hand_landmarker/web_js)).
- **Strict Mode:** React runs an extra setup and cleanup cycle in dev ([React StrictMode](https://react.dev/reference/react/StrictMode)), so use an `aborted` flag and full cleanup: `cancelAnimationFrame`, stop the tracks, `recognizer.close()`.
- **Visibility:** pause on `visibilitychange` (hidden).
- **State placement:** keep the recognizer, stream and engine in refs. Push HUD state to React at ≤ 10 Hz.

### 11.6 HUD

- **Placement:** a corner widget, ≤ 20% of the screen.
- **Contents:**
  - Optional mirrored camera thumbnail (toggle; off hides the video element but keeps inference running).
  - State chip: "Show your palm to start" → "Ready · 4 s" → "Hold fist… ◔" → "Timer started ✓".
  - Radial hold-progress ring.
  - Gesture legend (5 icons).
  - Hints: "Move closer" (hand bbox < 8%), "Turn on a light" (low confidence for 3 s), "One hand please".
- **Debug:** landmarks are drawn only when `NEXT_PUBLIC_GESTURE_DEBUG=true`.
- **Feedback:** every fired action produces a brief full-screen edge flash plus a soft click sound (respecting reduced motion) and an `aria-live` announcement, because the cook is often looking at the pan rather than the screen.
- **Camera indicator:** a persistent "Camera on" pill with a one-tap off switch.

### 11.7 Worker offload (P2)

The `GestureSource` interface allows a `WorkerGestureSource`:
- The main thread posts transferable `VideoFrame`/`ImageBitmap` objects, with one frame in flight.
- The worker is created with `new Worker(new URL('./gesture.worker.ts', import.meta.url), { type: 'module' })` and initialized with `forVisionTasks(base, true)`.
- Fishjam used this pattern in production ([Fishjam blog](https://fishjam.swmansion.com/blog/real-time-gesture-recognition-in-videoconferencing-4711855a1a53)).
- Module workers have a history of `importScripts` breakage, and a maintainer said 0.10.35 "should work" ([issue #5257](https://github.com/google-ai-edge/mediapipe/issues/5257)). `DrawingUtils` fails in workers. Test on Safari before switching.

### 11.8 Testability

- `GestureEngine` is a pure class: `update(result: GestureRecognizerResult-like, now: number)`. It takes no DOM or MediaPipe imports, so Vitest can drive it with synthetic landmark sequences in `features/gesture/__fixtures__/`.
- `KeyboardGestureSource` (Phase 0 mock) maps keys to `GestureAction`s so Cook Mode can be built before MediaPipe works.

## 12. UX rules (apply everywhere)

1. **Original before AI, always.** Anything Gemini *generated or transformed* carries a visible badge: "AI-adapted" on adaptations, "Read by AI, please confirm" on label and expiry drafts, "≈ estimate" on computed nutrition. Publisher content carries attribution instead.
2. **Confirm before save** for every AI extraction. Nothing from Gemini reaches the database without a user tap.
3. **Every gesture has a tap and a keyboard equivalent.** Gestures are never the only path, and hands-free is opt-in per session.
4. **Kitchen-distance readability in cook mode:**
   - Step text ≥ 32 px.
   - One step per screen.
   - Tap targets ≥ 25% of width for Prev and Next, and ≥ 56 px elsewhere.
   - Contrast ≥ WCAG AA. Dark theme default in cook mode.
5. **Colour is never the only signal.** Expiry bands also show text ("2 days"), and have/missing markers use icon + label.
6. **Feedback for hands-free actions** goes through three channels: visual flash, sound, and `aria-live` text. Respect `prefers-reduced-motion`.
7. **Progressive results.** Recipe search streams status messages and cards. Never show a spinner with no message for more than 2 s.
8. **Honest empty and error states:**
   - "We couldn't find this product" leads straight to the next fallback.
   - "Camera blocked" offers buttons and keyboard.
   - "Voice: Device" appears when ElevenLabs is unavailable.
9. **"Best before", not "Expires"**, unless Gemini classified the date as `expiry`/`use_by`. Show the raw printed text next to the parsed date.
10. **Allergy copy:** filters are strict, but the app always says "Always check product labels for allergens." Never claim a recipe is "safe".
11. **Units:** show the user's display unit and accept common abbreviations. Never show raw base units to users.
12. **Design deliverable:** produce a Figma file of the main screens (Today, Pantry, Scan, Recipes, Recipe detail with Original + AI-adapted, Cook mode + HUD) for the Best Design submission (§16).

## 13. Security and privacy

| Area | Rule |
|---|---|
| Secrets | Server-only. None use the `NEXT_PUBLIC_` prefix. `.env.production` lives on the VPS with `chmod 600` and is never baked into the image. Entire's secrets redaction is a bonus, not a control |
| AuthZ | `requireUser()` in every route handler and Server Action. Every SQL statement includes `user_id = ${user.id}`. IDs in URLs are always re-checked against the user, and a mismatch returns **404** (not 403) |
| Input validation | Zod on every body and query. Barcode digits 8–14. Text caps (TTS 2000, freeText 100). Image MIME allowlist and ≤ 4 MB each, ≤ 3 per request |
| LLM output | Treated as untrusted input: Zod-validated, values sanity-checked, pantry IDs verified, allergens re-checked in code, URLs verified by fetch |
| SSRF (recipe fetcher) | `server/recipes/safe-fetch.ts`: only `http(s)` on ports 80/443. Resolve DNS and **reject private, loopback, link-local and metadata IPs** (10/8, 172.16/12, 192.168/16, 127/8, 169.254/16, ::1, fc00::/7), re-checked on every redirect. Max 5 redirects, 5 s timeout, 2 MB body cap, `text/html` only |
| Rendering third-party HTML | Never `dangerouslySetInnerHTML` publisher HTML. Parse it to text. Gemini's Search Suggestions HTML is rendered **unmodified inside a sandboxed `<iframe srcdoc>`** (`sandbox="allow-popups allow-popups-to-escape-sandbox"`) **[VERIFY this satisfies the Grounding display terms]** |
| Camera and video | Frames are processed locally and never recorded, uploaded or stored. Model and WASM are self-hosted, so there are no third-party requests while hands-free is on. The camera starts only after an explicit toggle, a persistent indicator is shown, and tracks stop on toggle-off, page hide and route leave |
| Photos | Label and expiry photos go to Gemini through our server for one request and are **not persisted** (memory only). The UI copy says so |
| Headers | `Permissions-Policy: camera=(self), microphone=()`, `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff`, `Referrer-Policy: strict-origin-when-cross-origin`, `frame-ancestors 'none'`. CSP (P1): `script-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline' 'wasm-unsafe-eval'`; `img-src 'self' data: blob: https:`; `media-src 'self' blob:`; `connect-src 'self'`; `worker-src 'self' blob:`. The `'wasm-unsafe-eval'` source is needed for Emscripten WASM (general knowledge **[VERIFY]**) |
| Abuse and cost | Per-user rate limits (§7). TTS text cap. Discovery cache. Barcode cache and single-flight |
| Licensing and attribution | "Product data © Open Food Facts contributors, ODbL" in the footer and on product cards. OFF images are CC BY-SA. Recipe attribution and "View original" on every recipe |
| Data deletion | Settings → "Delete my data" deletes the `users` row (cascades) (P1) |

# Mise — agent rules

Spec: @SPEC.md (contracts in src/contracts/ win over prose). Tasks: @TASKS.md

## Commands
- npm run dev | npm run build | npm run typecheck | npm run lint | npm test | npm run test:db

## Hard rules
- Every route handler / Server Action starts with `const user = await requireUser()`; every SQL filters by user.id. Never read userId from the request.
- Secrets are server-only; never prefix with NEXT_PUBLIC_. Never log API keys or photos.

- LLM output is untrusted: zod-validate, re-check allergens with server/diet/checkDiet, verify pantry IDs and URLs.

- Small commits (each = Entire checkpoint). Conventional prefix: feat(ws-a): / fix(ws-c): / test: / contract:

## Conclusion

The riskiest parts of this build aren't gestures or auth. They are three LLM boundaries: finding real URLs, reading labels and dates, and adapting recipes. In each one, Gemini's output can be well-formed and still wrong. The spec therefore keeps Gemini out of every decision that has to be correct. Gemini finds candidate URLs, but the recipe content shown is whatever the publisher's own markup says, fetched and parsed by our code. Gemini reads a label, but a person confirms it. Gemini proposes a substitution, and `checkDiet` decides whether it is allowed. That split is also what lets three agents work in parallel safely, because the deterministic modules (units, GTIN, diet, scoring, timers, the gesture engine) are pure and testable against frozen contracts with no network. The two choices most worth revisiting after the event are the gesture thresholds in §11.4, which no published study validates, and how much publisher step text to store. That second one is a product and legal call, and the research could only partly settle it.

1536	
1537	- **Request:** `POST https://api.elevenlabs.io/v1/text-to-speech/{voice_id}/stream?output_format=mp3_44100_128`
1538	  - Header `xi-api-key`.
1539	  - Body `{ text, model_id: "eleven_flash_v2_5" }`. The API default model is `eleven_multilingual_v2`, so **always set the model explicitly**.
1540	  - `optimize_streaming_latency` is deprecated.
1541	  - Source: [Stream speech](https://elevenlabs.io/docs/api-reference/text-to-speech/stream)
1542	- **Why HTTP streaming:** it is the recommended mode "for cases where the input text is available up-front", which fits recipe steps. WebSockets are for incremental LLM text ([latency guide](https://elevenlabs.io/docs/eleven-api/guides/how-to/best-practices/latency-optimization.md)).
1543	- **Model choice:** Flash v2.5 has about 100 ms median model latency, up to 40,000 characters per request, 32 languages, and 50% lower per-character price. `eleven_turbo_v2_5` is deprecated ([Models](https://elevenlabs.io/docs/overview/models)).
1544	- **Cost:** Flash/Turbo API pricing is **$0.04 per 1K characters** ([API pricing](https://elevenlabs.io/pricing/api)). A 15-step recipe at about 150 characters per step comes to roughly $0.09, and caching makes repeat demos close to free.
1545	- **Route** (`app/api/tts/route.ts`):
1546	  1. Validate 1–2000 chars.
1547	  2. If there is no key, return 503 `UPSTREAM_UNAVAILABLE`.
1548	  3. Stream `r.body` through with `Content-Type: audio/mpeg` and `Cache-Control: private, max-age=86400`.
1549	  4. If the upstream response is non-2xx, return 502, and the client falls back.
