content.content:
## Installation

- **macOS/Linux/WSL:**
  ```
  curl -fsSL https://cli.tigerdata.com | sh
  ```
- **Windows (PowerShell):**
  ```
  irm https://cli.tigerdata.com/install.ps1 | iex
  ```

Other methods (Homebrew, apt, yum, `go install`) are also listed on the page.

## Authentication

```
tiger auth login
```

The page also documents `--headless`, which lets you authorize with a short code in a browser on any machine.

## tiger service create

The page's only example is:

```
tiger service create --name my-database
```

The page doesn't document the other flags, so run `tiger service create --help` for the full syntax.

## tiger service fork

The page doesn't document this command's syntax. It only lists `fork` as "Fork an existing service." It doesn't cover how to name the fork, which source service to use, or the `--now` and point-in-time options. Run `tiger service fork --help` for those details.

## tiger service list

```
tiger service list
```

The alias `ls` also works (`tiger service ls`).

## tiger db connection-string

The page documents this command as `tiger db uri`, with `connection-string` as an alias:

```
tiger db uri
tiger db connection-string
```

To target a specific service, the page says that anywhere a command takes a service, you can pass either its ID or its exact name as an argument. Its example is `tiger db psql my-api-db`, so the same positional form should apply here, though the page doesn't show it for this command. Names must match exactly, and a name matching more than one service is refused.

The global `--service-id <id>` flag is also available on all commands, and it takes an ID only, not a name:

```
tiger db uri --service-id <id>
```

The `TIGER_SERVICE_ID` environment variable and `tiger config set service_id` can also set a default service, which must be an ID.

You make it by copying the main database with the Tiger CLI, which isn't installed on this machine yet. The copy has to come from the main `mise-db` database, in the same Tiger account as `mise-db`. If Johnny already created `mise-db` in his account, you need access to that account or project first.

Run these in **PowerShell**:

1. **Install the CLI:**
   ```powershell
   irm https://cli.tigerdata.com/install.ps1 | iex
   ```
2. **Log in:**
   ```powershell
   tiger auth login
   ```
3. **Check whether `mise-db` exists:**
   ```powershell
   tiger service list
   ```
   If it's not listed and nobody has made one, create it with `tiger service create --name mise-db`. The free tier allows two databases per account, so `mise-db` plus this test copy uses both.
4. **Make the test copy (a "fork").** I couldn't find this command's exact options in the docs, so check them first:
   ```powershell
   tiger service fork --help
   ```
   Then fork `mise-db` and name the copy `mise-test`.
5. **Get its connection string:**
   ```powershell
   tiger db connection-string mise-test
   ```
6. **Put it in `.env.local`:**
   ```
   DATABASE_URL_TEST=postgres://tsdbadmin:...@host:port/tsdb?sslmode=require
   ```
7. **Run the database tests:**
   ```powershell
   npm run test:db
   ```
   This applies the migrations to the test copy, then runs Hang's database tests (finish-cooking transaction, finishing twice returns 409, per-user isolation, the nutrition aggregate).

Step 7 wouldn't have worked as the code stood: the migration script and the test runner both ignored `.env.local`, so they'd report `DATABASE_URL_TEST` missing even with it set. I fixed both using Node's built-in `.env` loader, with no new dependency. Normal tests still pass (343). The fix is on my local branch with the TTS fix, and neither is pushed.

Sources:

- [tiger cli (mcpservers.org)](https://mcpservers.org/es/servers/timescale/tiger-cli)

content.text:
Two things went wrong:
- **Partial command:** `fork mise-db` was typed without the `tiger service` in front, so PowerShell looked for a program called `fork`.
- **Wrong name:** your main database isn't called `mise-db`. It's **`hackcamp27`** (ID `vtb7pcud9m`).

Fork that one:

```powershell
tiger service fork hackcamp27 --name mise-test --no-set-default
```

`--no-set-default` keeps `hackcamp27` as your default database, so later `tiger` commands don't silently point at the test copy. The fork can take a few minutes; the command waits until it's done.

Then get its connection string:

```powershell
tiger db connection-string mise-test
```

If the string it prints has no password in it (no `tsdbadmin:something@`), check `tiger db connection-string --help` for an option that includes the password. The fork command has `--with-password`, so the connection-string command probably has something similar.

Put both strings in `.env.local`:

```
DATABASE_URL=<connection string for hackcamp27>
DATABASE_URL_TEST=<connection string for mise-test>
```

Then run:

```powershell
npm run test:db
```

content.content:
# claude-code review

Effort: medium (reused from last time). Type a level, for example `/code-review high`, to change it.

request changes: the SSRF guard can be bypassed, local dev with auth turned off breaks on every database write, and the search stream has a race and a cancellation leak.

- [medium] `src/server/recipes/safe-fetch.ts:122` and `:153`: the DNS rebinding check is a time-of-check/time-of-use gap. `assertUrlAllowed` resolves the host with `lookup()` and checks the IPs. Then `fetch(url.toString())` resolves the hostname a second time. A domain with a very short TTL can answer a public IP the first time and `127.0.0.1` or `169.254.169.254` the second time. Gemini returns the URLs and the publisher pages can be attacker-controlled, so this reopens the SSRF hole (§13) the module exists to close. Fix: pin the address you checked. Connect through an undici `Agent` with a custom `connect.lookup` that returns only the already-validated address, and keep the Host header and SNI set to the original hostname.

- [medium] `src/lib/current-user.ts:25`: `DEV_USER.id` (`00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000001`) is returned whenever `authDisabled` is true, but no migration or seed ever inserts it into `users`. With a real `DATABASE_URL` and no `AUTH0_DOMAIN`, every write that references the user fails its foreign key: `persistOriginal` (recipes.user_id), `createSession`, `setDiscoveryCache`. Every search candidate then shows up as `fetch_failed`, and "Start cooking" returns 500. Fix: in the `authDisabled` branch, run `INSERT INTO users (id, auth0_sub, email, display_name) VALUES (...) ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING` once, for example memoized in a module-level promise.

- [medium] `src/app/api/recipes/search/route.ts:116`: `if (stop()) return;` runs before `await persistOriginal(...)`, but `shown++` only runs afterwards, at `:145`. With 5 workers, several can pass the check while `shown` is still below `maxResults`. All of them then persist and emit a candidate. For example, with `maxResults=1`, two workers finish `processExtracted` at the same moment and both stream a candidate, so the client gets more results than it asked for. Fix: reserve the slot synchronously before the await, with `if (shown >= body.maxResults) return; shown++;` (or a separate `reserved` counter), and release it if the persist fails.

- [medium] `src/lib/http.ts:60`: `ndjsonResponse` has no `cancel()` handler and passes no abort signal to `producer`. `SearchStream` aborts the previous search each time the user submits again. On the server, `controller.enqueue` then throws inside the worker's `try`. The `catch` calls `write` again, which throws again. Meanwhile the other workers keep fetching up to 12 publisher pages and running extraction, which may include the Gemini fallback, with nobody reading the results. That wastes rate-limit budget and API cost. Fix: add `cancel() { aborted = true }`, make `write` a no-op once aborted, and expose the `aborted` flag (or an `AbortSignal`) to the producer so the search loop can stop.

- [low] `src/server/recipes/safe-fetch.ts:67`: `isBlockedIp` only matches the literal first hextet `fe80`. Link-local is `fe80::/10`, which covers `fe80` through `febf`, so `fe90::1` and `febf::1` pass. The IPv4 list also leaves out `100.64.0.0/10` (CGNAT, which holds the metadata service on some clouds), and NAT64 `64:ff9b::/96` isn't decoded. Fix: test `/^fe[89ab]/` on the first hextet, and add `100.64.0.0/10` (plus `198.18.0.0/15` and `224.0.0.0/4`) to the IPv4 checks.

- [low] `src/app/api/tts/route.ts:24`: `checkRateLimit` uses up a token before `Body.safeParse` at `:27`. A client that sends malformed bodies, such as empty text, drains the per-user 60/min budget and gets 429s on valid requests. `recipes/search/route.ts` has the same ordering. Fix: validate the body first, then check the rate limit.

- [low] `src/server/cook/finish.ts:92`: this rebuilds a `PantryItem` from raw rows by hand, about 30 lines. It duplicates `rowToPantryItem` in `src/server/recipes/pantry-view.ts` and loses fields, using `expiryDate: null` and `allergenTags: []`. The two mappings will drift whenever the pantry shape changes. Fix: `SELECT *` and map through `rowToPantryItem(row, tz)`, or call `listPantryByIds`/`listPantryForMatching` with `tx`.

- [low] `src/server/recipes/pantry-view.ts:132`: `getProfileFilters` queries `users` again for diets, allergens and tz right after `requireUser` upserted and returned that same row. That costs every recipes, adapt, search and finish-preview request one extra round trip. Fix: add `diets, allergens` to `requireUser`'s `RETURNING` clause and to `AppUser`, then drop `getProfileFilters`.

- [low] `src/app/api/recipes/search/route.ts:68`: `let cached = urls != null;` is followed by `else { cached = true; }` at `:77`, which sets the same value twice. Separately, `mustUse` at `:54` is computed for every request but only read when `mustUsePantryItemIds` is provided. Fix: use `const cached = urls != null;` and compute `mustUse` inside the `if (body.mustUsePantryItemIds)` block.

- [low] `scripts/migrate.mjs:25` and `src/lib/db.ts:20`: `ssl: 'require'` is hard-coded, so `npm run migrate`, `test:db` and the app all fail against a local Postgres or Docker database without TLS, a common setup for teammates. Fix: leave `ssl` unset, since postgres.js honours `?sslmode=require` in the URL, or read it from an env flag.

lines: +A hands-free cooking companion: scan pantry items, find recipes that match what you have and your diet, then cook with gesture/voice control. Built with Next.js (App Router), Auth0, Postgres/Tigerdata, Gemini, MediaPipe, and ElevenLabs TTS.
+Full product spec, data model, and API contracts live in [`SPEC.md`](./SPEC.md).
+This also runs `scripts/copy-assets.mjs` (`postinstall`), which copies the MediaPipe and zxing WASM binaries into `public/` so the browser loads them locally instead of from a CDN.
+The app currently runs against stub data where backend work is still in progress:
+- `src/lib/current-user.ts` returns a placeholder user until Auth0 wiring lands.
+- Cook mode can run against fixtures by setting `NEXT_PUBLIC_COOK_FIXTURES=true`.
+- `/api/tts` needs `ELEVENLABS_API_KEY` set to return real audio; without it, voice features won't produce speech.

+There is no `.env.example` yet — add required secrets (Auth0, database, Gemini, ElevenLabs) to a local `.env` as the corresponding workstreams land. See `SPEC.md` §8 for the full environment variable list.
+- `src/app` — routes (App Router): landing page, `(app)` shell (Today, Pantry, Recipes, Cook, Settings, Onboarding), API routes.
+- `src/contracts` — shared domain/API types and fixtures used across workstreams before real endpoints land.
+- `src/lib` — server-only helpers (auth, db, etc. as they're added).

+This repo uses [Entire](./CLAUDE.md) for branch/trail-based review on top of Claude Code. See `CLAUDE.md` for the exact workflow, and `hang.md` / `jerry.md` / `johnny.md` for each workstream's task breakdown.

# claude-code review

Effort level: none was given, so this reused medium, the level you typed last time. Typing a level (for example `/code-review high`) changes it.

request changes: the SSRF guard can be bypassed with IPv4-mapped IPv6 addresses written in hex, and several paths give wrong or stalled results.

- [high] `src/server/recipes/safe-fetch.ts:71-74`: the URL parser rewrites `http://[::ffff:127.0.0.1]/` or `[::ffff:169.254.169.254]` into hex form (`::ffff:7f00:1`, `::ffff:a9fe:a9fe`). `lookup` hands that literal back unchanged. Then `ipv4ToInt(clean.slice(7))` gets `"7f00:1"`, returns `null`, and the function falls through to `return false`, so the address is allowed. A publisher page, or a redirect `Location`, pointing at that host reaches loopback or the cloud metadata service. Fix: parse the last 32 bits of `::ffff:` addresses in hex as well as dotted form. Also block `::/96` (IPv4-compatible) and `64:ff9b::/96`, or simply block any `::ffff:` address that won't parse. Add a test for `[::ffff:7f00:1]`.
- [medium] `src/server/recipes/safe-fetch.ts:187-188`: `clearTimeout(timer)` runs as soon as headers arrive, so reading the body (lines 215-224) has no deadline at all. A publisher that sends headers and then drips bytes holds a search worker forever. With 5 workers, a few such URLs stall `/api/recipes/search` and the `done` event never comes. Fix: keep the timer running until the body is fully read, or set a separate overall deadline and abort the reader when it passes.
- [medium] `src/server/cook/finish.ts:92-123`: finish builds its own pantry list with `expiryDate: null, daysToExpiry: null` and no quantity filter. `matchIngredients` therefore loses FEFO ordering and accepts expired items. The pantry item matched at finish can differ from the one in `getFinishPreview` (`sessions.ts:202`, which uses `listPantryForMatching`), so the kcal/protein logged differs from the suggestion the user confirmed. Fix: call `listPantryForMatching(userId, tz, new Date(), 200)` here instead of re-implementing the row mapping.
- [medium] `src/app/api/recipes/search/route.ts:49,54-56`: `listPantryForMatching(user.id, profile.tz)` uses the default `limit = 25`. With more than 25 pantry items, explicitly passed `mustUsePantryItemIds` beyond the first 25 are silently left out of `ctx.expiring`, and matching treats the user's own items as missing. Fix: pass `200` as the adapt and preview routes do, or load `mustUsePantryItemIds` with `listPantryByIds`.
- [low] `src/app/api/recipes/[id]/adapt/route.ts:18-33`: the rate-limit token is spent before the 404 and the "Nothing to adapt" 409 checks. This goes against the "validate before spending tokens" rule this branch applied to search and TTS, so repeated no-op adapt clicks lock the user out for a minute. Fix: move `checkRateLimit` to just before `requestAdaptation`.
- [low] `src/app/api/recipes/[id]/route.ts:17-18`: the path `id` (here, in adapt, and in `cook/sessions/[id]/*`) is passed to SQL without UUID validation. A malformed id like `/api/recipes/abc` makes Postgres throw `invalid input syntax for type uuid`, which `handleRouteError` turns into a 500 instead of a 404. Fix: `z.string().uuid().safeParse(id)` and return NOT_FOUND on failure.
- [low] `src/app/api/cook/sessions/[id]/finish/route.ts:9-10`: the schema accepts `servingsEaten > servingsCooked`, for example cooked 1 and eaten 5. That logs five servings of kcal for a single cooked portion. Fix: add a `.refine((b) => b.servingsEaten <= b.servingsCooked)` check.

- [high] `src/server/recipes/adapt.ts:42-70` — `validateAdaptation` runs `checkDiet` only on each `sub.substitute`. It never checks `output.ingredients`, the full updated list that gets stored and cooked, or the `stepChanges[].newText`. For a user with a peanut allergen, the model can add "2 tbsp peanut butter" to `ingredients` with `changed: true`, or put it into a step, while keeping the substitution text clean. Validation passes, `insertAdaptation` stores it, and the cook flow shows it. That breaks the "ONLY enforcement mechanism" rule in `check.ts`. Fix: also run `checkDiet(output.ingredients.map(i => i.text), filters)` and check the step texts, and add any violations to `errors`.
- [medium] `src/app/api/recipes/[id]/adapt/route.ts:37-48` — `findMatchingAdaptation` returns a stored adaptation only by comparing the set of missing ingredients. It does not re-check it against the user's current `diets`/`allergens`. A user who adapted a recipe, then added a dairy allergen or the vegan diet, gets the old adaptation with its butter substitute. Fix: run `checkDiet` on the cached adaptation's ingredient texts and skip it (generate a new one) if it fails.
- [medium] `src/server/recipes/match.ts:7` — The `SYNONYMS` key `cilantro: ['coriander leaf']` (line 22) runs after `coriander: ['cilantro']`. Its `aliasToCanonical.set('cilantro','cilantro')` overwrites `cilantro→coriander`. So `canonical('cilantro')` is `'cilantro'` and `canonical('coriander')` is `'coriander'`, and a recipe calling for "cilantro" never matches a pantry item named "coriander" (or the reverse). Fix: merge both into one entry, `coriander: ['cilantro', 'coriander leaf']`, and add a match test for it.
- [low] `src/server/cook/finish.ts:75` — `SELECT * FROM pantry_items WHERE user_id = …` has no `ORDER BY`. The preview path (`listPantryForMatching`) orders by `expiry_date NULLS LAST, normalized_name` before the stable sort and `slice(0, 200)`. When items share an expiry date, or there are more than 200 items, the transaction can match different pantry rows than the preview showed. The logged kcal/protein then differs from what the dialog suggested. Fix: use the same `ORDER BY` in the in-transaction query.
- [low] `src/server/recipes/match.ts:94` — The doc comment says "Exact normalizedName, then synonyms, then token-subset". In fact `usable.find((item) => namesMatch(...))` takes the first item in FEFO order that matches by any of the three rules. Ingredient "chicken thigh" therefore matches a sooner-expiring "boneless chicken thigh stock"-style token-subset item before an exact "chicken thigh" row. - [medium] `src/app/api/recipes/[id]/adapt/route.ts:37-48` — `findMatchingAdaptation` returns a stored adaptation only by comparing the set of missing ingredients. It does not re-check it against the user's current `diets`/`allergens`. A user who adapted a recipe, then added a dairy allergen or the vegan diet, gets the old adaptation with its butter substitute. Fix: run `checkDiet` on the cached adaptation's ingredient texts and skip it (generate a new one) if it fails.
- [medium] `src/server/recipes/match.ts:7` — The `SYNONYMS` key `cilantro: ['coriander leaf']` (line 22) runs after `coriander: ['cilantro']`. Its `aliasToCanonical.set('cilantro','cilantro')` overwrites `cilantro→coriander`. So `canonical('cilantro')` is `'cilantro'` and `canonical('coriander')` is `'coriander'`, and a recipe calling for "cilantro" never matches a pantry item named "coriander" (or the reverse). Fix: merge both into one entry, `coriander: ['cilantro', 'coriander leaf']`, and add a match test for it.
- [low] `src/server/cook/finish.ts:75` — `SELECT * FROM pantry_items WHERE user_id = …` has no `ORDER BY`. The preview path (`listPantryForMatching`) orders by `expiry_date NULLS LAST, normalized_name` before the stable sort and `slice(0, 200)`. When items share an expiry date, or there are more than 200 items, the transaction can match different pantry rows than the preview showed. The logged kcal/protein then differs from what the dialog suggested. Fix: use the same `ORDER BY` in the in-transaction query.
- [low] `src/server/recipes/match.ts:94` — The doc comment says "Exact normalizedName, then synonyms, then token-subset". In fact `usable.find((item) => namesMatch(...))` takes the first item in FEFO order that matches by any of the three rules. Ingredient "chicken thigh" therefore matches a sooner-expiring "boneless chicken thigh stock"-style token-subset item before an exact "chicken thigh" row. Fix: search the exact matches, then the synonym matches, then the token-subset matches, each in FEFO order, or fix the comment.
- [low] `src/app/api/recipes/search/route.ts:94` — `safeFetchHtml(url)` is called without the stream `signal`. When the client aborts (for example, a new search replaces the old one), up to 5 in-flight fetches, extractions and `persistOriginal` writes keep running for the abandoned request. Fix: pass the signal through to the fetch and combine it with the timeout controller using `AbortSignal.any`.
- [low] `src/server/cook/finish.ts:10-20` — `SessionRow` and the inline `CookingSession` mapping at lines 137-150 copy `SessionRow` and `toCookingSession` from `sessions.ts:18-63`. `finish.ts:155` (`export type { RecipeStep, Substitution }`) is an unused re-export, and `variants[0]!` is used even though `variant` is already in scope. Fix: export `toCookingSession`/`SessionRow` from `sessions.ts`, reuse them, and delete the dead re-export.
- [low] `src/server/recipes/pantry-view.ts:124` — `getPantryItem` and `listPantryByIds` (line 132) are never called. `sessions.ts:7,224` only imports `listPantryByIds` so it can re-export it, and nothing imports that. This is dead code. Fix: delete them until the pantry routes need them.

content.text:
All the merging is done and `dev` is pushed (`b0aefb2`). Every check passes on it: typecheck, lint, 370 tests, the 6 database tests against `mise-test`, and the build. The main database is migrated, and every key in your `.env.local` is set, so you can test the real app with real sign-in.

**What `dev` now has:**
- Hang's code merged in, using main's scaffold, contracts and UI kit.
- Three review rounds' worth of fixes:
  - **Security:** the recipe fetcher can no longer be tricked into calling internal addresses.
  - **Safety:** AI adaptations can't sneak an allergen into the ingredients or steps.
  - **Reliability:** recipe search doesn't overshoot its result count or keep running after you start a new search, and finish cooking matches the same pantry items its preview showed.
- My earlier fixes: `/api/tts` returns 401 when signed out and is limited to 60 requests a minute; `npm run test:db` and migrations now read `.env.local`.

**Left for Hang:** a few non-urgent cleanups in his recipe matching and finish-cooking code (match-order comment, some duplicated code, unused functions).

**Before you test**
- Check out `dev`:
  ```
  git switch dev
  git pull origin dev
  npm install
  ```
- In the Auth0 dashboard, make sure the app allows `http://localhost:3000/auth/callback` (callback URL) and `http://localhost:3000` (logout URL and web origin).
- Start it with `npm run dev` and open http://localhost:3000. It must be port 3000 to match `APP_BASE_URL`.
- Add `NEXT_PUBLIC_GESTURE_DEBUG=true` to `.env.local` if you want the pose readout under the HUD.

**What to test**
1. **Sign in:** click "Sign in", log in through Auth0, and you should land in the app. Log out and back in. Then, while signed out, open http://localhost:3000/today directly: it should send you to the login page.
2. **Recipe search (Hang's code, real Gemini):** go to Recipes and run a search. Status messages and recipe cards should stream in, each card showing the source site and author, and "View original" should open the publisher's page. Start a second search straight away: the first should stop, and only the new results should appear.
3. **Recipe detail:** open a recipe. You should see the original first with attribution. If ingredients are missing, try "Suggest an AI adaptation": it should appear in a separate card with an "AI-adapted" badge.
4. **Cook mode, real data:** press Cook on a recipe. It should create a session and open `/cook/<id>`.
   - Start cooking, step with ←/→, start a timer with T, read aloud with R. The badge should say "Voice: ElevenLabs" now that your key is set.
   - Reload mid-recipe: it should offer "Resume at step N", and the timer should show the right time.
   - Hands-free: hold ☝️ (next) and 🤟 (back) still, fist toggles the timer, victory reads aloud. It's always armed now, so no palm step.
   - Do 30 s of stirring and chopping in front of the camera: nothing should trigger.
   - Note the FPS with the processor on GPU, then on CPU (⚙ settings).
5. **Finish cooking:** on the last step, press "Finish cooking".
   - Servings eaten can't go above servings cooked.
   - Confirm takes you to `/today` with a toast like "Logged 1 serving · … kcal".
   - Pressing Finish again on the same session should say it's already finished.

**What you can't test yet:** your pantry is empty, and Johnny's pantry, scan and Today pages are still placeholders. So recipes will show every ingredient as missing, finish won't deduct anything, and `/today` won't show the logged meal. The meal is still saved; you just can't see it until Johnny's work lands.

Tell me what breaks and I'll fix it. When you're happy with `dev`, I can merge it to main through a trail.
